title: Small Bathroom Design: Layouts, Ideas & Remodel Tips
h1: Small Bathroom Design: Layouts, Dimensions and Ideas That Make a Tiny Bath Feel Luxurious
description: Small bathroom design made simple: common layouts with dimensions, clearances, renter-friendly ideas, remodel costs and finishes that make it feel bigger.
excerpt: Layouts with real dimensions, the clearances that matter, renter-friendly fixes and remodel ideas that make a small bathroom feel bigger and more luxurious.
image_alt: Small bathroom design with a floating vanity, round mirror and glass shower panel in soft neutral tile
key_takeaways: The classic small full bath is 5x8 ft; aim for 30 in. of clear space in front of the toilet and vanity.
A shallower 16–18 in. vanity, a sliding door or a glass shower panel often fixes a cramped layout without moving plumbing.
Renters get the biggest impact from a high-mounted shower curtain, a larger mirror, warm high-CRI bulbs and matching hardware.
Low-contrast, tone-on-tone finishes and large-format tile make a small bathroom look bigger.
Typical small bathroom remodels range from about $5,000 for an update to $30,000+ for a layout change.

faq.q: What is the standard size of a small bathroom?
faq.a: The most common small full bathroom in the US is 5 by 8 feet, or 40 square feet, with a 60-inch tub across the back wall and the vanity and toilet along one long wall. Compact apartment baths can be 5 by 7 feet, and powder rooms with only a toilet and sink are often 3 by 6 to 4 by 5 feet.

faq.q: How can I make my small bathroom look bigger?
faq.a: Reduce contrast with tone-on-tone colors, use large-format tile with fewer grout lines, swap a shower curtain or framed door for clear glass, hang a large mirror and choose a floating vanity that shows more floor. Mounting the curtain rod close to the ceiling and adding good lighting also make the room feel taller and more open.

faq.q: What is the best layout for a 5x8 bathroom?
faq.a: For most 5x8 bathrooms the best layout keeps the standard arrangement: a 60-inch tub or walk-in shower across the 5-foot back wall, with the vanity and toilet side by side along one 8-foot wall. That keeps all plumbing on one wall. Improve it with a shallower vanity, a sliding or outswing door and a glass shower panel.

faq.q: How can renters update a small bathroom?
faq.a: Renters can replace the mirror, hang a shower curtain near the ceiling, change bulbs to warm high-CRI LEDs, swap towel bars and cabinet pulls, add over-the-toilet shelving and cover dated floors with a washable runner or peel-and-stick tiles. Keep original parts to reinstall and get permission before painting or using adhesives.

faq.q: How much does it cost to remodel a small bathroom?
faq.a: Typical US ranges are roughly $500 to $2,500 for a cosmetic refresh, $5,000 to $12,000 for a mid-range update with a new vanity, toilet and fan, $12,000 to $30,000 for a full gut remodel in the same layout, and $30,000 or more when plumbing is moved or luxury materials are used. Local labor costs and building rules change these numbers.
